correctness.rationale: After absorbing the minus sign in the first quadric, Jacobian dependence at a fiber point means its support lies in a single eigenvalue block. On a size-two block the first quadric gives two points; eliminating a coordinate leaves exactly the nondegenerate quadratic in the three complementary coordinates, even if a different block is repeated. A size-three block leaves a binary quadratic with two distinct factors; the restrictions of the first quadric to the two hyperplanes are nondegenerate because the two complementary eigenvalues differ, and the intersection is the smooth conic on the repeated block. In the plane t4=0, t0+t1+t2+t3=0, each triple and each choice of two disjoint pairs determines one projective point of exactly that pattern; sizes 4 and (3,2) would force the zero vector. Hence the ten triple incidences are precisely pair-in-triple and the other 15 crossings are ordinary double. A transverse general line meets ten open line strata. The determinant's five linear factors have pairwise brackets ti-tj, giving the square with no other factor. Independently, projection to the fixed smooth quadric threefold gives a P1-bundle away from the simultaneous zeros of yi^2-y3^2 for i=0,1,2, and a P2 over each of those points. On y3=1 these are the 16 distinct points with y0,y1,y2=±1 and y4=±2. The coefficient differences are local coordinates at these points, so the total incidence hypersurface in the product with the quadric is smooth there and elsewhere. This gives e(X)=2(4-16)+3·16=24, separately from the frozen stratified and Chern computations. The independent exact incidence replay (/workspace/replay/independent_checks.py, incidence) accounts for all 45 pairs of lines at 10 triple and 15 double points. The replay is not a certificate of the complex local geometry. The divisor comparison is specifically for the binary-quintic discriminant, not an unspecified critical-value scheme.
